newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps - mogas up $5 on cracker problems.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps - mogas up $5 on cracker problems.

text.p: Gasoline swaps jumped $5 or so on tight supplies exacerbated by problems with catalytic crackers at three NWE refineries and the continued strong U.S demand.
Heavy fuel swaps were firm, but fairly quiet with low sulphur swaps showing a $1 gain or so. Brent CFDs were a few cents firmer.

Gasoline was bounced higher with news that one of Shell's Pernis, Rotterdam cat crackers (28,000 bpd) would be out of action for the months of August, September and October, that BP/Texaco's 55,000 bpd cat cracker at its Nerefco, Rotterdam unit would be out of action for a few days and also that the Coryton, U.K. 60,000 bpd cat cracker managed by BP and Mobil was shut down and would not be open until the middle to end of next week.

August gasoline was seen trading at $210.00, $211.00 and $212.00, about $5 stronger than Thursday's levels with September concluded at $198.50 and $198.75. Dealers also said August/September traded at $11.
Brent CFDs were a few cents firmer with August 4-8 pegged at +14 cents against September Brent from +10 cents with August 11-15 at flat from -2 cents.
August 18-22 was put at -6/7 cents, unchanged, while August 25-29 at -11 cents was a cent or so stronger.
Traders said August 11-15 traded at September flat and at September + one cent. A roll Augsut 11-15 versus 18-22 was done at +12.
Heavy fuel swaps for August were pegged around $92 with September in contango by 50-75 cents. Low sulphur swaps moved a touch higher with August talked around $94.00-94.50.
